questions.problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=x-2y+\frac{3}{2},\,y(1)=\frac{1}{2}
$$

We wish to approximate the solution using the $2$-step Adams-Bashforth-Moulton method. Given that the step size is $Δx=\frac{1}{2},$ and that one preliminary step has already been computed using the Runge-Kutta method, complete the second row of the table below.

*Hint: The corrector equation of the two-step Adams-Bashforth-Moulton method is defined as*

$$
Δy=\frac{1}{12}(5{y}_{p}^{′}+8{y}^{′}-{y}_{-1}^{′})\cdot Δx
$$

*where ${y}_{p}$ denotes the predictor at the current step, and ${y}_{-1}^{′}$ is the estimated slope at the previous point.* 

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $Δ{y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}^{′}$ | $Δy$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $\frac{1}{2}$ | $\frac{3}{2}$ | $-$ | $-$ | $-$ | $\frac{9}{16}$ |
| $\frac{3}{2}$ | $\frac{17}{16}$ | $\frac{7}{8}$ | $\frac{9}{32}$ | $\frac{43}{32}$ | $\frac{13}{16}$ | {{field-1}} |
questions.worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
{y}^{′}=f(x,y),\,y(a)=c,
$$

the $2$-step Adams-Bashforth-Moulton (ABM2) method with step size $Δx$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Predictor} & : & Δ{y}_{p} & =\frac{1}{2}(3{y}^{′}-{y}_{-1}^{′})\cdot Δx, \\ \text{Corrector} & : & Δy & =\frac{1}{12}(5{y}_{p}^{′}+8{y}^{′}-{y}_{-1}^{′})\cdot Δx,\end{aligned}
$$

where

- ${y}^{′}=f(x,y)$ is the estimated slope at the current point $(x,y),$

- ${y}_{-1}^{′}=f({x}_{-1},{y}_{-1})$ is the estimated slope at the previous point (${x}_{-1},{y}_{-1}),$ and

- ${y}_{p}^{′}=f({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{p})$ is the estimated slope at the predicted new point $({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{p})=(x+Δx,y+Δ{y}_{p}).$

Looking at the partially filled table, we note the following:

- From the second row, the slope at the current point $(x,y)=(\frac{3}{2},\frac{17}{16})$ is ${y}^{′}=\frac{7}{8}.$

- From the first row, the slope at the previous point $({x}_{-1},{y}_{-1})=(1,\frac{1}{2})$ is ${y}_{-1}^{′}=\frac{3}{2}.$

- From the second row, the slope at the predicted new point $({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{p})$ is ${y}_{p}^{′}=\frac{13}{16}.$

Now, we compute $Δy$ using the corrector equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =\frac{1}{12}(5{y}_{p}^{′}+8{y}^{′}-{y}_{-1}^{′})\cdot Δx \\  & =\frac{1}{12}(5\cdot \frac{13}{16}+8\cdot \frac{7}{8}-\frac{3}{2})\cdot \frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{24}\cdot \frac{153}{16} \\  & =\frac{51}{128}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the completed row is as given below.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $Δ{y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}^{′}$ | $Δy$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $\frac{1}{2}$ | $\frac{3}{2}$ | $-$ | $-$ | $-$ | $\frac{9}{16}$ |
| $\frac{3}{2}$ | $\frac{17}{16}$ | $\frac{7}{8}$ | $\frac{9}{32}$ | $\frac{43}{32}$ | $\frac{13}{16}$ | $\frac{51}{128}$ |

questions.worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
{y}^{′}=f(x,y),\,y(a)=c,
$$

the $2$-Step Adams-Bashforth-Moulton (ABM2) method with step size $Δx$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Predictor} & : & Δ{y}_{p} & =\frac{1}{2}(3{y}^{′}-{y}_{-1}^{′})\cdot Δx, \\ \text{Corrector} & : & Δy & =\frac{1}{12}(5{y}_{p}^{′}+8{y}^{′}-{y}_{-1}^{′})\cdot Δx,\end{aligned}
$$

where

- ${y}^{′}=f(x,y)$ is the estimated slope at the current point $(x,y),$

- ${y}_{-1}^{′}=f({x}_{-1},{y}_{-1})$ is the estimated slope at the previous point (${x}_{-1},{y}_{-1}),$ and

- ${y}_{p}^{′}=f({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{p})$ is the estimated slope at the predicted new point $({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{p})=(x+Δx,y+Δ{y}_{p}).$

We're told that the first step is calculated using the Runge-Kutta Method, resulting in 

$$
y(1)≈\frac{4}{3}.
$$

Now, we'll continue from this point, using the $2$-step ABM method.

First, we compute the value of ${y}^{′}$ according to the given rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =x(2y-x-1) \\  & =1\cdot (2\cdot \frac{4}{3}-1-1) \\  & =\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

So, we add this to our table.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $Δ{y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}^{′}$ | $Δy$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $1$ | $0$ | $-$ | $-$ | $-$ | $\frac{1}{3}$ |
| $1$ | $\frac{4}{3}$ | $\frac{2}{3}$ |  |  |  |  |

From the first row of the table, we see that the slope at the previous point $({x}_{-1},{y}_{-1})=(0,1)$ is ${y}_{-1}^{′}=0.$

Next, we compute $Δ{y}_{p}$ using the predictor equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}Δ{y}_{p} & =\frac{1}{2}(3{y}^{′}-{y}_{-1}^{′})\cdot Δx \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(3\cdot \frac{2}{3}-0)\cdot 1 \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

We add this to our table.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $Δ{y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}^{′}$ | $Δy$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $1$ | $0$ | $-$ | $-$ | $-$ | $\frac{1}{3}$ |
| $1$ | $\frac{4}{3}$ | $\frac{2}{3}$ | $1$ |  |  |  |

So, the coordinates of the predicted new point are

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{\text{new}} & =x+Δx=1+1=2, \\ {y}_{p} & =y+Δ{y}_{p}=\frac{4}{3}+1=\frac{7}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Let's add the second value to the table.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $Δ{y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}^{′}$ | $Δy$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $1$ | $0$ | $-$ | $-$ | $-$ | $\frac{1}{3}$ |
| $1$ | $\frac{4}{3}$ | $\frac{2}{3}$ | $1$ | $\frac{7}{3}$ |  |  |

Hence, the slope at this predicted point is

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{p}^{′} & ={x}_{\text{new}}(2{y}_{p}-{x}_{\text{new}}-1) \\  & =2\cdot (2\cdot \frac{7}{3}-2-1) \\  & =\frac{10}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

We can add this to our table.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $Δ{y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}^{′}$ | $Δy$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $1$ | $0$ | $-$ | $-$ | $-$ | $\frac{1}{3}$ |
| $1$ | $\frac{4}{3}$ | $\frac{2}{3}$ | $1$ | $\frac{7}{3}$ | $\frac{10}{3}$ |  |

Finally, we compute $Δy$ using the corrector equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =\frac{1}{12}(5{y}_{p}^{′}+8{y}^{′}-{y}_{-1}^{′})\cdot Δx \\  & =\frac{1}{12}(5\cdot \frac{10}{3}+8\cdot \frac{2}{3}-\frac{4}{3})\cdot 1 \\  & =\frac{1}{12}\cdot 22 \\  & =\frac{11}{6}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the completed row is as given below.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $Δ{y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}^{′}$ | $Δy$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $1$ | $0$ | $-$ | $-$ | $-$ | $\frac{1}{3}$ |
| $1$ | $\frac{4}{3}$ | $\frac{2}{3}$ | $1$ | $\frac{7}{3}$ | $\frac{10}{3}$ | $\frac{11}{6}$ |

The value of $x$ in the next row is ${x}_{\text{new}}=1.$ To get the value of $y$ in the next row, we add $Δy$ to $y:$

$$
{y}_{\text{new}}=y+Δy=\frac{4}{3}+\frac{11}{6}=\frac{19}{6}
$$

Adding these results to our table gives the following:

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $Δ{y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}^{′}$ | $Δy$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $1$ | $0$ | $-$ | $-$ | $-$ | $\frac{1}{3}$ |
| $1$ | $\frac{4}{3}$ | $\frac{2}{3}$ | $1$ | $\frac{7}{3}$ | $\frac{10}{3}$ | $\frac{11}{6}$ |
| $2$ | $\frac{19}{6}$ |  |  |  |  |  |

Therefore, we conclude that $y(2)≈\frac{19}{6}.$

$$

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $Δ{y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}^{′}$ | $Δy$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $-1$ | $-1$ | $-$ | $-$ | $-$ | $-\frac{1}{4}$ |

where

- ${y}^{′}=f(x,y)$ is the estimated slope at the current point $(x,y),$

- ${y}_{-1}^{′}=f({x}_{-1},{y}_{-1})$ is the estimated slope at the previous point (${x}_{-1},{y}_{-1}),$ and

- From the second row, the slope at the current point $(x,y)=(\frac{1}{4},-\frac{5}{4})$ is ${y}^{′}=-1.$

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $Δ{y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}^{′}$ | $Δy$ |

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{\text{new}} & =x+Δx=1+1=2, \\ {y}_{p} & =y+Δ{y}_{p}=\frac{8}{3}+8=\frac{32}{3}.\end{aligned}

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $Δ{y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}^{′}$ | $Δy$ |

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $Δ{y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}^{′}$ | $Δy$ |

questions.problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=x-y-10,\,y(1)=2
$$

To approximate the solution, one step of the Runge-Kutta method has already been computed, resulting in the following estimate:

$$
y(2)≈-\frac{9}{2}
$$

Use the $2$-Step Adams-Bashforth-Moulton Method with one step to approximate $y(3).$

*Hint: The corrector equation of the two-step Adams-Bashforth-Moulton method is defined as*

$$
Δy=\frac{1}{12}(5{y}_{p}^{′}+8{y}^{′}-{y}_{-1}^{′})\cdot Δx
$$

*where ${y}_{p}$ denotes the predictor at the current step, and ${y}_{-1}^{′}$ is the estimated slope at the previous point.*
questions.worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
{y}^{′}=f(x,y),\,y(a)=c,
$$

the $2$-Step Adams-Bashforth-Moulton (ABM $2$-step) Method with step size $Δx$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Predictor} & : & Δ{y}_{p} & =\frac{1}{2}(3{y}^{′}-{y}_{-1}^{′})\cdot Δx, \\ \text{Corrector} & : & Δy & =\frac{1}{12}(5{y}_{p}^{′}+8{y}^{′}-{y}_{-1}^{′})\cdot Δx,\end{aligned}
$$

where

- ${y}^{′}=f(x,y)$ is the estimated slope at the current point $(x,y),$

- ${y}_{-1}^{′}=f({x}_{-1},{y}_{-1})$ is the estimated slope at the previous point (${x}_{-1},{y}_{-1}),$ and

- ${y}_{p}^{′}=f({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{p})$ is the estimated slope at the predicted new point $({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{p})=(x+Δx,y+Δ{y}_{p}).$

Before we start, let's add the initial condition data and Runge-Kutta step data to a table.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $Δ{y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}^{′}$ | $Δy$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $2$ |  | $-$ | $-$ | $-$ | $-$ |
| $2$ | $-\frac{9}{2}$ |  |  |  |  |  |

Now, since we want to find the value of $y$ at $x=3,$ we will use a step size of

$$
Δx=3-2=1.
$$

First, we compute the values of ${y}^{′}$ at each point according to the given rule:

- The slope at the previous point $({x}_{-1},{y}_{-1})=(1,2)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{-1}^{′} & ={x}_{-1}-{y}_{-1}-10 \\  & =1-2-10 \\  & =-11.\end{aligned}
$$

- The slope at the current point $(x,y)=(2,-\frac{9}{2})$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =x-y-10 \\  & =2-(-\frac{9}{2})-10 \\  & =-\frac{7}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

We add these values to our table.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $Δ{y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}^{′}$ | $Δy$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $2$ | $-11$ | $-$ | $-$ | $-$ | $-$ |
| $2$ | $-\frac{9}{2}$ | $-\frac{7}{2}$ |  |  |  |  |

Next, we compute $Δ{y}_{p}$ using the predictor equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}Δ{y}_{p} & =\frac{1}{2}(3{y}^{′}-{y}_{-1}^{′})\cdot Δx \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(3\cdot (-\frac{7}{2})-(-11))\cdot 1 \\  & =\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

We add this to our table.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $Δ{y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}^{′}$ | $Δy$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $2$ | $-11$ | $-$ | $-$ | $-$ | $-$ |
| $2$ | $-\frac{9}{2}$ | $-\frac{7}{2}$ | $\frac{1}{4}$ |  |  |  |

So, the coordinates of the predicted new point are

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{\text{new}} & =x+Δx=2+1=3, \\ {y}_{p} & =y+Δ{y}_{p}=-\frac{9}{2}+\frac{1}{4}=-\frac{17}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Let's add the second value to the table.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $Δ{y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}^{′}$ | $Δy$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $2$ | $-11$ | $-$ | $-$ | $-$ | $-$ |
| $2$ | $-\frac{9}{2}$ | $-\frac{7}{2}$ | $\frac{1}{4}$ | $-\frac{17}{4}$ |  |  |

Hence, the slope at this predicted point is

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{p}^{′} & ={x}_{\text{new}}-{y}_{p}-10 \\  & =3-(-\frac{17}{4})-10 \\  & =-\frac{11}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

We can add this to our table.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $Δ{y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}^{′}$ | $Δy$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $2$ | $-11$ | $-$ | $-$ | $-$ | $-$ |
| $2$ | $-\frac{9}{2}$ | $-\frac{7}{2}$ | $\frac{1}{4}$ | $-\frac{17}{4}$ | $-\frac{11}{4}$ |  |

Finally, we compute $Δy$ using the corrector equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =\frac{1}{12}(5{y}_{p}^{′}+8{y}^{′}-{y}_{-1}^{′})\cdot Δx \\  & =\frac{1}{12}(5\cdot (-\frac{11}{4})+8\cdot (-\frac{7}{2})-(-11))\cdot 1 \\  & =\frac{1}{12}\cdot (-\frac{123}{4}) \\  & =-\frac{41}{16}.\end{aligned}
$$

We add this to our table.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $Δ{y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}^{′}$ | $Δy$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $2$ | $-11$ | $-$ | $-$ | $-$ | $-$ |
| $2$ | $-\frac{9}{2}$ | $-\frac{7}{2}$ | $\frac{1}{4}$ | $-\frac{17}{4}$ | $-\frac{11}{4}$ | $-\frac{41}{16}$ |

The value of $x$ in the next row is ${x}_{\text{new}}=3.$ To get the value of $y$ in the next row, we add $Δy$ to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\  & =-\frac{9}{2}+(-\frac{41}{16}) \\  & =-\frac{113}{16}.\end{aligned}
$$

Adding these results to our table gives the following:

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $Δ{y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}^{′}$ | $Δy$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $2$ | $-11$ | $-$ | $-$ | $-$ | $-$ |
| $2$ | $-\frac{9}{2}$ | $-\frac{7}{2}$ | $\frac{1}{4}$ | $-\frac{17}{4}$ | $-\frac{11}{4}$ | $-\frac{41}{16}$ |
| $3$ | $-\frac{113}{16}$ |  |  |  |  |  |

Therefore, we conclude that $y(3)≈-\frac{113}{16}.$
